text:
Jordan's week runs on two tracks that keep touching each other: the practical machinery of a life mid-pivot, and the slower work of noticing what's actually changed underneath it.

It opens on the 14th with the lease renewal — signed one day before deadline, a year at $150 more, from a window table at Groundwork. Jordan knows the timing is odd given that Northlight, if it comes through, could upend the commute entirely, but the decision reads as a refusal to let an unconfirmed job dictate a housing choice already settled back in August. The same entry carries the recurring office dream, now in its third iteration — except this time Jordan finds the stairs and walks out, no flooding, no sideways elevator. Jordan won't claim the dream means anything causal, but notes the shift anyway. The entry closes on the real throughline of the week: not that the job situation resolved (it didn't — Jordan got "parked in the holding pen"), but that something changed regardless, traced back to a pattern of handing the heavy thing to someone else instead of carrying it alone — Dev, Mom, Lena. The timing collision is also named plainly: Priya starts managing Jordan on the 21st, the Northlight onsite is the 24th, three days later.

The 15th and 16th are quieter, more constructive. Jordan writes documentation for a dashboard at a company that may not want them past October, framing it as work that outlives tenure rather than personal investment. Then comes the real repair: the free-play review screen gets rebuilt, stripping out the "trophy-case" framing — no more highlight reels, no more marks that are pre-judged as good. The rebuild is described as costly (more code thrown out than written) but clarifying, and it's explicitly tied back to something Dev's session on the 3rd cracked open. Dev appears again on the 16th, three days from a gig, running the setlist clean; Jordan brings their father's old guitar picks, and Dev's casual absorption of them into their case lands harder than expected. Mika's open-mic text triggers Jordan's familiar avoidance script ("not ready," "next month") — but Jordan catches it this time, names it as the same voice that doubted Northlight, and signs up anyway for the 27th.

The 17th turns inward: building the interview deck surfaces that Jordan's journal has been quietly functioning as a design log, and re-reading old entries changes the story Jordan thinks they're telling — from defensive ("I missed this but it's not that bad") to plain ("I missed this and here's what I learned"). Lena offers help; Jordan declines in the only way currently available. The Priya meeting is now four days out, Northlight three days after that, and the fear from the 11th is acknowledged as still present, unresolved, not going anywhere by week's end.
